$schema_note: Capability matrix for visual-prompt-forge adapters. Generator models churn monthly. When you re-verify an adapter, bump its model_version and last_verified date here, then reconcile the prose adapter file. This file is the single source of truth for 'what each generator can do'; the .md files are the how-to-prompt guidance. max_prompt_words is a ceiling, not a target: an adapter .md may recommend a narrower range, but it may never advertise more than the ceiling. tools/validate_capabilities.py enforces that relationship and checks that each .md documents the aspect_param named here.

generators.notes: Short high-signal phrases. 100 words is the ceiling, past which signal drops off; the adapter recommends 40 to 80. --cref/--sref for series consistency.
Natural-language descriptive. Stronger text rendering than MJ but still treat on-screen copy as a separate compositing pass.
Best in-class text rendering. The exception case: if a shot truly needs baked text, Ideogram is the fallback. Default is still composite-after.
Paragraph-form, instruction-following. Tolerates the most context. Good for complex compositions described in sentences.
Fast, cheap, strong editing/consistency via reference images. Good for high-volume iteration. Parameter name is camelCase here, unlike the fal.ai models; it ignores --ar.
Strong photoreal and bilingual text. Competitive on character consistency.
Default motion model. Best camera-motion realism per dollar on fal.ai, strongest image-to-video (start/tail frame). 5s or 10s. Reach for this first; escalate only for what it cannot do.

Dialogue and lipsync. Only adapter that generates synchronised native audio in the same pass. Strongest prompt adherence and physics; highest cost. ~8s. Spoken lines go in the prompt; on-screen text still does not.
Multi-shot sequences in a single generation with subject consistency across cuts. Use when consecutive beats share one subject and should feel like one take. Up to ~4 cuts per generation.
Budget, fast iteration. Use to block out camera move, framing, and timing across cheap drafts, then re-roll the keeper on Kling, Veo, or Seedance. Draft tier, not finals.
